answer: Because the atlas ordering is published with the beacon batch, the ridge audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. A farm that floods the queue early as a result gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 28% of the queue is processed in arrival order. Honest users pay that once, farms 37 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
